messages:
alex: Quick sketch — propose a "hot-path evacuation" policy for when a tenant's primary model instance/group is saturated. Idea: automatic, tier-aware variant handoff with region-first preference. tradeoffs below. thoughts?
priya: +1 on region-first. main runtime concerns: KV cache warmup + token continuity if we swap into a variant mid-request.
alex: Right — plan is to only auto-fallback for new requests, not mid-response. existing streams keep running. we avoid KV migration, just warm caches lazily and mark as cold for first few tokens.
marco: We need circuit-breaker and a metric to track "evacuated_requests" per-hour per-tenant. Also alert when >1% of p95 latency is coming from cross-region fallbacks.
janelle: From product side, teams want a toggle in Console: "Evacuation mode: off / prefer-local-variant / allow-cross-region". Default: prefer-local-variant for enterprise tiers, off for free tier. UI should show number of fallbacks and avg added latency.
sam: API idea: add header & config flags. Example: `Prefer-Variant-Fallback: policy=prefer_local; max_latency_ms=150; allowed_tiers=premium,enterprise`
priya: Implementation details: runtime router should try 1) local compatible variant (same region, same precision/quantization family), 2) local lower-cost variant if tenant allows quality degrade, 3) cross-region equivalent variant, 4) fail or queue based on tenant QoS. Each step needs explicit telemetry.
marco: Also: a soft quota penalty if tenant keeps forcing cross-region — helps protect capacity. And record `fallback_reason` tags in traces: "saturated_primary", "quota_blocked", "manual_override".
janelle: UX for rollouts: we need a per-tenant canary checkbox to enable auto-evacuation for a subset of traffic. Show expected latency delta and cost delta before you flip.
alex: Agreed. For safety, default behavior should be conservative: only evict to compatible models that are marked as "auto-evacuate-eligible". Ops can tag model variants in the Console.
sam: Console backend will need a small API surface: PATCH /tenants/:id/routing_fallback { policy, allowed_variants, cross_region_allowed }
priya: Runtime note: when falling back to lower-capacity variant, we should shrink max tokens for that request if we detect memory pressure. That avoids OOMs on smaller variants.
marco: We must also simulate traffic in perf-env before enabling for a tenant. Add a chaos test that marks primary as saturated and measure evacuation success rate.
alex: Minimal config snippet (proposal):
```
fallback_policy:
  mode: prefer_local
  tiers_allowed: [enterprise, premium]
  compatible_only: true
  max_added_latency_ms: 250
  telemetry_tags: [evac_policy, region, tenant_tier]
```
priya: +1. Also expose a per-route override header for internal services: `X-Redwood-Evac-Mode: force-local|force-cross|off`. Only allowed with admin scopes.
janelle: Docs + in-console warnings must call out quality regressions when downgrading model family. Maybe auto-run a small prompt-set eval when tenant opts-in to allow downgrade, surface the score change.
sam: We should add a new Console chart: "Evacuation events" with breakdown by target variant, avg added latency, and cost delta. Also searchable by time range/tenant.
marco: Ops: add playbook entry — if cross-region fallbacks spike >5% sustained, escalate to capacity team. Possibly auto-scale dedicated pools.
alex: Ok will draft an RFC with flow diagrams and telemetry schema. Next steps: priya + sam to map to runtime APIs, marco to draft SRE alerts, janelle to design console toggles.
priya: I'll prototype routing decision order in the router shim this week.
sam: I'll stub the Console API and chart placeholders.
marco: I'll author the chaos test and Prometheus/alert rules.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline triggered: link https://ci.internal/redwood/pipelines/evac-policy-prototype (build 42) :rocket:
alex: thanks — moving to RFC stage. tagging @product-reviewers for visibility. :thumbsup:
